records.description: The 2026 MOFCOM Scholarship is a Chinese government aid programme that provides advanced study opportunities in diverse fields for developing countries, aimed at strengthening their human resource capacity. It is open to postgraduate studies (master's and doctoral degrees) and is administered in two tracks: MOFCOM-40, 40 projects led directly by MOFCOM, and the MOFCOM - China Scholarship Council (CSC) Joint Program, for which applicants register on the CSC study-in-China portal using institution code 00010 and submit materials to their target universities. Applicants who have received any type of Chinese Government scholarship funding within the past three years are not eligible for this round.

eligibility: Postgraduate applicants for master's and doctoral degrees
Senior officials of the Sierra Leonean government, university faculty, or corporate executives, aged 45 or younger, with at least 3 years of work experience
Academic background: bachelor's degree for master's applicants, master's degree for doctoral applicants
Good health, with a physical examination at the 34th Military Hospital or Jui Hospital, with the medical examination form signed and verified by a Chinese doctor
Academic performance: minimum GPA of 3.25 on a 4-point scale or 4.0 on a 5-point scale
Priority: HSK Level 3 or higher (Chinese proficiency is an advantage)
Applicants who received any type of Chinese Government scholarship funding within the past three years are not eligible for this round
benefits: Advanced study at the master's and doctoral level in China under a government aid programme
MOFCOM-40: study on one of 40 projects led by MOFCOM
MOFCOM-CSC Joint Program: study through the CSC portal with institution code 00010
selection_criteria: Embassy-preselection interview and shortlist based on academic and interview performance
Applicants who are not invited to the interview are automatically disqualified
Final admission decision rests with the university's admission committee
official.application_process: Applicants choose either MOFCOM-40 (apply for one project only, contact the university contacts in the admission brochure, and complete online registration on university portals if applicable) or MOFCOM-CSC (search independently for university international admissions contacts, submit materials to university emails, and complete registration on the CSC portal and the university portals). Materials in PDF format plus Appendix 3 are emailed to sl@mofcom.gov.cn by 12 May 2026, with the mail subject 'MOFCOM-40, GPA and Scale (e.g., 3.25/4.0), Applicant Name, WhatsApp Number' or 'MOFCOM-CSC, GPA and Scale (e.g., 3.25/4), Applicant Name, WhatsApp Number' as appropriate. Shortlisted applicants are notified for an interview in late May 2026, admission results are announced around July-August 2026 and successful applicants receive visa assistance.
key_dates: Submission to the embassy deadline: 12 May 2026

deadlines.label: Submission to the embassy
deadlines.note: Email materials in PDF plus Appendix 3 to sl@mofcom.gov.cn by 12 May 2026. Incomplete or overdue applications are rejected.

verification.deadline_note: No fixed application cycle; the notice states 12 May 2026 for the 2026 recruitment only, and does not publish a recurring deadline.
verification.application_cycle: Annual notice; the 2026 recruitment set 12 May 2026 as the embassy submission deadline and July-August 2026 for results.
verification.tuition_coverage_note: Not stated on this notice. The notice states that the final admission decision rests with the university's admission committee and directs applicants to each university's admission brochure and the MOFCOM aid programme platform for details, so the award value and coverage are published by the individual university, not on this page.
verification.status_note: Status computed at research time (10 October 2026). The 2026 recruitment closed on 12 May 2026 and no 2027 notice has been published, so the programme is marked CLOSED.

source_citations.claim: 2026 MOFCOM Scholarship notice: two tracks (MOFCOM-40 with 40 MOFCOM-led projects, and MOFCOM-CSC with CSC institution code 00010); eligibility of government officials, university faculty and corporate executives aged 45 or younger with at least 3 years of work experience; GPA 3.25/4.0 or 4.0/5.0 minimum; HSK 3 as a priority; those funded by a Chinese Government scholarship within the past three years are not eligible; PDF materials plus Appendix 3 emailed by 12 May 2026; interview notification in late May 2026; results around July-August 2026; the following documents are required: application form, two recommendation letters (one employer and one academic professor), authenticated degree certificate and transcript, personal statement of at least 1,000 words, Foreigner Physical Examination Form, passport copy valid at least 18 months, CV, police clearance and the Applicant Information Form (Appendix 4).

Degree certificate (bachelor's or master's) stamped by the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
Transcript with GPA score, with the same authentication
Personal statement (including a study/research plan of at least 1,000 words)
Foreigner Physical Examination Form (Appendix 3), with a physical check at the 34th Military Hospital or Jui Hospital and a Chinese physician signature
Passport copy, valid at least 18 months; official or diplomatic passports are not accepted

applicant_utility.description: MOFCOM is a two-track scholarship, and choosing the wrong track wastes the cycle: MOFCOM-40 is 40 MOFCOM-led projects for which you apply to one project only, while MOFCOM-CSC routes you through the China Scholarship Council portal using institution code 00010 plus the target university's own portal. Everything - documents, the physical examination and the embassy submission - was due by 12 May 2026.
eligibility_tips: The profile requirement is specific: senior government officials, university faculty or corporate executives, aged 45 or younger with at least 3 years of work experience. Recent graduates without that profile are not in scope.

Check the three-year exclusion rule: recipients of any Chinese Government scholarship funding within the past three years are not eligible for this round (those who graduated in 2023 or earlier and previously received funding are eligible).
Academic performance is screened numerically: GPA of at least 3.25 on a 4-point scale or 4.0 on a 5-point scale. HSK Level 3 is a priority criterion, and Chinese proficiency is an advantage.
application_tips: For MOFCOM-40, contact the university contacts listed in the admission brochure and apply to exactly one project; for MOFCOM-CSC, find the university international admissions contacts yourself and register on both the CSC portal and the university portal.

Get your degree certificate and transcript stamped by the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation - this dual authentication is a common point of failure and takes weeks.

Do the physical examination early at the 34th Military Hospital or Jui Hospital: the Foreigner Physical Examination Form requires a Chinese physician's signature and is emailed as part of the same package.

Use the exact email subject format the notice specifies ('MOFCOM-40, GPA and Scale (e.g., 3.25/4.0), Applicant Name, WhatsApp Number' or 'MOFCOM-CSC, GPA and Scale (e.g., 3.25/4), Applicant Name, WhatsApp Number'), and include Appendix 3 with the PDF materials.
Keep the hard copies: documentation for the scholarship programme is submitted only by email and online system, and applicants keep the hard copies themselves.
If shortlisted for the late-May 2026 interview, bring the original copies of your application materials on the day; uninvited applicants are automatically disqualified.
documents: Two recommendation letters (one employer, one academic professor)
Personal statement with a study/research plan of at least 1,000 words
Passport copy valid at least 18 months (not an official/diplomatic passport)
mistakes_to_avoid: Applying to more than one MOFCOM-40 project; each applicant applies to one project only.
Submitting an overdue or incomplete application, which the notice states is rejected outright.
Using an official or diplomatic passport, or a passport with less than 18 months of validity.
Missing the Chinese physician signature on the Foreigner Physical Examination Form.
Expecting the embassy to guarantee admission: the embassy recommends qualified applicants and the final admission decision rests with the university's admission committee.
Falsifying documents: the notice warns that in previous years degrees were revoked due to falsified transcripts.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: 2026 recruitment: embassy submission deadline 12 May 2026, interview notification in late May 2026, results around July-August 2026. Watch for the next year's notice, which follows the same pattern; the same document set and authentication requirements will apply.

records.description: UCAS offers the 2026 Chinese Government Scholarship (Chinese University Program) for international students applying for master's and doctoral programmes, administered jointly by the China Scholarship Council and UCAS. The scholarship covers tuition, monthly living expenses and on-campus accommodation, with medical insurance paid once; one applicant may apply for the scholarship for only one programme at UCAS, applications must be submitted by 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time), and the award may continue for a maximum of three years of master's study (without extension) or four years of doctoral study, extendable by up to one year subject to CJNS-80 reward criteria.

eligibility: Students with high-school qualifications should be aged under 25; those with a master's degree under 35; those with a bachelor's degree under 40
Must not be receiving any other sponsorship or financial support while studying
Applicants must be enrolled as full-time students, and may not take other jobs (including on-campus, internship or online jobs)
Applicants not currently pursuing a degree programme in China
benefits: Tuition exemption of 40,000 RMB/year for doctoral students and 30,000 RMB/year for master's and general visiting scholars

Monthly living stipend of 5,000 RMB for doctoral students (4,000 RMB from the university and 1,000 RMB from the supervisor/institute) and 3,500 RMB for master's and general visiting students (3,000 RMB from the university and 500 RMB from the supervisor/institute)
Free accommodation on the Beijing campus, or a subsidy of up to 700 RMB/month for master's and general visiting students and up to 1,000 RMB/month for doctoral and senior visiting students
Medical insurance of 800 RMB per person per year

Award period of 36 months for master's and general visiting students (no extension) and 36 months for doctoral and senior visiting students, extendable by up to 12 months subject to CJNS-80 reward criteria
selection_criteria: Comprehensive review and admission by UCAS after the CSC review of eligibility
Applications are evaluated in the CSC system and the UCAS system
official.application_process: Applicants must apply online on the CSC system (CGS information platform at studyinchina.csc.edu.cn or campuschina.org) with agency number 80001, and separately apply online on the UCAS system. Applications must be completed before the deadline of January 31st, 2026 (Beijing Time). One applicant may apply for the scholarship for only one programme at UCAS.
official.duration: Master's: 36 months (no extension). Doctoral: 36 months, extendable by up to 1 year
key_dates: Call published: 2025 year, in the 2026 CGS window (not later than 1 March 2026)
Award period: 36 months for master's (no extension) and 36 months for doctoral (extendable by up to 1 year)

source_citations.claim: 2026 CGS (Chinese University Program) at UCAS: tuition exemption of 40,000 RMB/year for doctoral and 30,000 RMB/year for master's/general visiting; 600 RMB application fee subsidy; living stipend of 5,000 RMB/month for doctoral (4,000 university + 1,000 supervisor/institute) and 3,500 RMB/month for master's/general visiting (3,000 + 500); free accommodation on the Beijing campus or a subsidy of up to 700/1,000 RMB per month; medical insurance of 800 RMB per person; award period of 36 months for master's (no extension) and 36 months doctoral, extendable by up to 12 months subject to CJNS-80; age limits of 25 (under-25 high-school), 35 (master's) and 40 (bachelor's for doctoral); proficient in English or Mandarin; no other sponsorship; full-time study only; not currently pursuing a degree in China; deadline of January 31st, 2026 (Beijing Time); apply in both the CSC system with agency number 80001 and the UCAS system; one scholarship application per programme at UCAS.

applicant_utility.description: This is a Type-A Chinese Government Scholarship for a specific university, so you apply twice: once in the China Scholarship Council system under agency number 80001, and again in UCAS's own system. Both must be completed before 31 January in Beijing Time, and you may only use the scholarship for one programme at UCAS.
eligibility_tips: Check the age brackets before you apply: under 25 with high-school qualifications, under 35 for master's applicants, and under 40 for bachelor's applicants seeking doctoral study.
The 'no other sponsorship or financial support' and 'no other jobs' clauses are strict: you cannot hold an internship, an on-campus job or online work while on this award.
If you are already enrolled in a degree programme in China, you are excluded - finish or leave that programme first.
application_tips: Use agency number 80001 when registering in the CSC system; using the wrong agency number routes your application outside UCAS's pool.

Remember the split of your stipend: 5,000 RMB/month for doctoral students of which 4,000 comes from the university and 1,000 from your supervisor or CAS institute (3,500/month for master's students, 3,000 + 500), so the supervisor's willingness matters.

Budget beyond the stipend: the tuition exemption is 40,000 RMB/year for doctoral and 30,000 RMB/year for master's study, accommodation in Beijing is free, and medical insurance is paid once at 800 RMB per person.

Plan the award period: master's study is funded for 36 months with no extension, while doctoral study is 36 months extendable by up to one year subject to the CJNS-80 reward criteria - so complete within the window or keep the CJNS-80 evidence.

Your obligations continue after award: annual reviews by UCAS, publication of your research with UCAS as the academic institution, acknowledgement of the CGS funding, and use of the doctoral or master's award only within the specified award period. Failure to comply may mean the cost is recovered from you.
mistakes_to_avoid: Applying only in the CSC system or only in the UCAS system; both are required.
Applying for more than one programme at UCAS with the scholarship.
Taking a job or internship during the award, which is explicitly prohibited.
Relying on the stipend alone in Beijing: the 5,000 RMB/month doctoral figure is split, and 3,500 RMB/month applies to master's students.
Missing the Beijing Time deadline of 31 January 2026; both systems must be complete before then.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: The 2026 call closed on 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time) and no 2027 call is published at research time. Diarise 31 January each year to check whether the new call has been posted.
